Count CLOSURE samples per scale value, and single-peaked ones

Source: R/count.R
closure_count_details.Rd

closure_count_details() goes beyond closure_count_all(): for each scale value and each count, it says in how many CLOSURE samples the value occurs that many times. It does this over all samples and over the single-peaked ones, without generating any sample.

A sample is single-peaked if its counts rise to a maximum and then fall, with ties allowed but no dip at all. This needs no cutoff for what counts as a peak, unlike the shape classes of closure_generate().

The function settles whether any single-peaked sample has the reported statistics, and what the counts of every such sample would have to be. It also gives the range of each scale value's count across all samples, like modality_counts in the output of closure_generate(). All of this is exact, and it remains feasible at sample sizes where generating the samples is not. It takes about one and a half times as long as closure_count_all().

Like closure_count_all(), it assumes a single item per respondent.

Usage

closure_count_details(
  mean,
  sd,
  n,
  scale_min,
  scale_max,
  rounding = "up_or_down",
  threshold = 5
)

Arguments

mean

String (length 1). Reported mean.

sd

String (length 1). Reported sample standard deviation.

n

Numeric (length 1). Reported sample size.

scale_min, scale_max

Integers (length 1 each). Minimum and maximum of the scales to which the reported statistics refer.

rounding

String (length 1). Rounding method assumed to have created mean and sd. See Rounding options, but also the Rounding limitations section below. Default is "up_or_down" which, e.g., unrounds 0.12 to 0.115 as a lower bound and 0.125 as an upper bound.

threshold

Numeric (length 1). Number from which to round up or down, if rounding is any of "up_or_down", "up", and "down". Default is 5.

Value

Named list of three tibbles:

  • metrics_main (one row): samples_all, the number of all samples, as returned by closure_count_all(), and samples_single_peak, the number of single-peaked samples. Both are doubles.

  • modality_counts (one row per scale value): value, then count_lo, count_hi, and count_mean, the smallest, largest, and average count of the value across all samples; then the same over the single-peaked samples (single_peak_count_lo etc.). They are NA if there are no such samples.

  • frequency_dist (one row per scale value and count that occurs in any sample): value, count, n_samples, the number of samples in which the value occurs count times, and n_samples_single_peak, the same among the single-peaked samples.

Sample numbers above about 1.8e19 are capped there.

Examples

# Some samples are single-peaked:
closure_count_details(
  mean = "3.5",
  sd = "1.2",
  n = 70,
  scale_min = 1,
  scale_max = 5
)
#> $metrics_main
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   samples_all samples_single_peak
#>         <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1        7912                 892
#> 
#> $modality_counts
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   value count_lo count_hi count_mean single_peak_count_lo single_peak_count_hi
#>   <dbl>    <int>    <int>      <dbl>                <int>                <int>
#> 1     1        0       13       5.06                    1                    8
#> 2     2        0       27       9.94                    5                   17
#> 3     3        0       43      15.9                     7                   27
#> 4     4        0       57      23.2                    16                   40
#> 5     5        0       27      15.9                     8                   21
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: single_peak_count_mean <dbl>
#> 
#> $frequency_dist
#> # A tibble: 172 × 4
#>    value count n_samples n_samples_single_peak
#>    <dbl> <int>     <dbl>                 <dbl>
#>  1     1     0       630                     0
#>  2     1     1       672                     7
#>  3     1     2       714                    35
#>  4     1     3       756                    89
#>  5     1     4       798                   152
#>  6     1     5       838                   224
#>  7     1     6       833                   241
#>  8     1     7       754                   134
#>  9     1     8       630                    10
#> 10     1     9       504                     0
#> # ℹ 162 more rows
#> 

# Samples exist, but none is single-peaked:
closure_count_details(
  mean = "4.00",
  sd = "1.73",
  n = 5,
  scale_min = 1,
  scale_max = 7
)$metrics_main
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   samples_all samples_single_peak
#>         <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1           2                   0
